question: What is the primary anatomical purpose of a tracheostomy tube?

options.C: Deliver medications directly to the lungs

explanation: A tracheostomy creates an artificial airway directly into the trachea, bypassing any blockage located in the upper respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: A patient with severe Guillain-Barré syndrome needs a tracheostomy mainly for which reason?

options.A: Correcting severe metabolic acidosis from kidney failure
options.B: Treating an acute bacterial pneumonia infection
options.C: Managing thick tracheal secretions and respiratory weakness
options.D: Preventing sudden cardiac arrest during sleep

explanation: Neuromuscular disorders cause weak coughs and poor breathing, requiring an artificial airway for secretion clearance and ventilation support. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which tracheostomy component is removed immediately after the tube is inserted?
explanation: The obturator guides the outer cannula during insertion and must be removed right away so the patient can breathe through the tube. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is the main function of the inner cannula in a tracheostomy set?

options.A: It guides the doctor during the initial surgical cut
options.B: It inflates to stop liquid from entering the lungs
options.C: It connects the breathing machine to the patient
options.D: It can be removed and cleaned to prevent mucus plugs

explanation: The inner cannula collects dried secretions and can be taken out for cleaning or replacement without disturbing the outer tube. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h2)

question: What critical equipment must always remain at the bedside of a patient with a new tracheostomy?

options.A: A sterile surgical scalpel for emergency re-incision
options.C: A spare tracheostomy tube of the same size
options.D: A container of sterile normal saline for drinking

explanation: An identical spare tube must be readily available at the bedside for immediate reinsertion if the current tube accidentally falls out. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h3)

question: When should suctioning be applied during tracheostomy care?

options.A: While pushing the catheter down the tube
options.B: Before the patient is given any extra oxygen
options.D: Continuously during both insertion and withdrawal

explanation: Suctioning during withdrawal protects the delicate lining of the trachea from trauma and tissue damage. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to suction a tracheostomy tube for longer than fifteen seconds?

options.A: It forces mucus deeper down into the tiny air sacs
options.B: It removes too much oxygen and causes low blood oxygen levels
options.C: It permanently damages the automatic cough reflex nerves
options.D: It causes the inner cannula to melt from the vacuum pressure

explanation: Prolonged suctioning removes air along with secretions, which rapidly depletes oxygen reserves and leads to dangerous hypoxia and heart arrhythmias. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the primary emergency action when a newly placed tracheostomy tube accidentally falls out?

options.A: Cover the open neck hole with a dry gauze pad
options.B: Administer rescue breaths using an oxygen mask on the face
options.C: Wait calmly for the surgical team to arrive at the bedside
options.D: Attempt immediate reinsertion using a spare tube

explanation: A fresh tracheostomy tract closes rapidly, making immediate tube reinsertion vital to maintain a patent airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h5)

question: What physical sign indicates that air has leaked into the tissues surrounding the tracheostomy stoma?

options.A: Loud whistling sounds coming from inside the mouth
options.B: A crackling feeling under the skin when touched
options.C: Bright red blood dripping continuously from the outer edge
options.D: A sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure reading

explanation: Subcutaneous emphysema creates crepitus, a characteristic crackling sensation felt when palpating the skin around the neck due to trapped air. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h5)

question: What must a patient demonstrate before a tracheostomy tube can be safely removed?

options.A: Normal breathing rates while sleeping for two full nights
options.B: Effective cough and ability to protect their own airway
options.C: Ability to speak clearly without any finger covering
options.D: Complete healing of the neck skin incision scar

explanation: Decannulation requires proof that the patient can clear their own secretions and breathe independently without aspirating. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h6)

question: How is the open tracheostomy wound typically managed after the tube is removed?

options.A: Left completely open to the air without any dressing
options.B: Covered with an airtight dressing to heal on its own
options.C: Sutured tightly closed right away by the surgeon
options.D: Packed with antiseptic gauze until new skin grows

explanation: An occlusive dressing seals the stoma to prevent air leakage, allowing the tissue to close naturally over time. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h6)
